<meta>This page continues the theological exploration of "Amen" as a title for Christ. The previous page established "Amen" as a name for the God of Truth in Isaiah 65:16; this page transitions into the legal and covenantal reasons why Christ is called "the Amen" and "the True Witness."</meta>

# A M E N.

e. In such a way is Christ the faithful and true witness, and thus the Amen, that he has many who have testified and shown of him that he is the Amen. *Deuteronomy 18:18; Psalms 14:4; Joel 2:34; Luke 24:24-27, 44; John 1:6-19; John 6:39-46; Acts 1:8; Acts 10:43; Revelation 19:10; etc.*

f. He is a confirming witness through the power of his convincing teaching, miracles, death, and resurrection, with so many clear and soul-stirring proofs of faith, that Israel in his time, having taken his message to heart, not only had to stand amazed, but also be fully convinced of his credibility. *John 5:33; etc.*

John [the Baptist] was indeed his witness; he himself was even more his own witness; the Father had given testimony of him at his baptism; likewise all the prophets unanimously; and so heaven and earth came into agreement.

g. He is the witness who at the same time testifies and exhorts and binds man to his duty; he does not merely <term>testify<note>original Greek: *martyrei*</note></term>, but <term>testifies solemnly<note>original Greek: *diamartyrei*</note></term>, as he consistently did throughout the course of his prophetic office on earth.

I have taken even more things into consideration, for I read in *1 Corinthians 1:6: "even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you."*

Regarding this, I wrote in my exposition of the first letter of Paul to the Corinthians, page 27:

*The root word <term>testimony<note>original Greek: *martyrion*</note></term> comes from <term>witness<note>original Greek: *martyr*</note></term>.*

*The testimony of Christ can thus be understood as referring to Christ himself, who testified and gave witness (John 1:4; 5:33; and 8:12; 1 Timothy 6:13; Hebrews 3:14) and thereafter also the testimony that the prophets, apostles, John the Baptist, and even the Father himself gave of him (Psalm 40:8; John 1:6, 7-29; and 5:39-46; Acts 1:8 and 10; Revelation 19:10).*

*Christ was, as appears from 1 Timothy 6:13, such a witness who testified with power of words, spirit, and life, wonders and signs, and confirmed his teaching and testimony with his blood and death. He is a sworn witness who testified before the judge Pontius Pilate. John 18:37, 38.*

Here, what the learned Campegius Vitringa <note>A prominent Dutch theologian (1659–1722) known for his work on the synagogue and the book of Isaiah.</note> noted in *Sacred Observations, pages 3, 15, etc.*, comes wonderfully to my aid, where he writes:

*What is particularly relevant here: <term>The Amen<note>original Greek: *to Amēn*</note></term> does not merely signify a witness who declares that a matter is so, but also a sworn witness who, having answered "Amen," prayed to someone who had adjured or put him under oath.*

<margin>Sworn witnesses.</margin>
For we have clearly enough from the laws of the Hebrews that witnesses were adjured [placed under oath] by the judges, and that they had to say "Amen" upon this adjuration. There is a passage in the Codex <term>Shevu'ot<note>original Hebrew: "Oaths," a tractate of the Talmud dealing with legal oaths.</note></term>, chapter 4, section 3: *How is the oath of witnesses? If someone says to two people, "I adjure you," and if they say "Amen," they are bound or obligated.* Maimonides <note>The influential 12th-century Jewish philosopher and jurist.</note> writes in his *Treatise on <term>Oaths<note>original Hebrew: *Shevu'ot*</note></term>, chapter 11*: *The judges say to him, the witness, "We adjure you by Jehovah the God of Israel, or by him whose name is Merciful"; then this witness answers, "Amen." Therefore the witness was adjured, and the witness swore solemnly.*

<column-break/>

How these things are to be applied to Christ must subsequently be investigated. From eternity there has been a <term>counsel<note>original Hebrew: *etzah*</note></term>, a covenant between the Father and the Son. And in every covenant there is an <term>oath<note>original Hebrew: *shevu'ah*</note></term>, which follows the testimony or adjuration. He who is first in the covenant testifies or adjures; the second swears. In the agreement made between the Father and the Son, the Father was the first, the Son the second: it was therefore the Father’s part to adjure, and the Son’s to swear. The Father says to the Son, "I adjure you, my Son, by my holiness, that you redeem those from the human race whom I have written as your heirs"; the Son says <term>Amen<note>original Hebrew: *Amen*</note></term>, "Your will, O God, I do gladly" (*Psalm 40:7*). The Son is regarded as a <term>servant<note>original Hebrew: *eved*</note></term>, the Father as <term>Lord<note>original Hebrew: *Adon*</note></term>. That the servant swears loyalty to his Lord, we know from the history of Abraham and Eliezer (*Genesis 24*); compare what is written in *Isaiah 49:6-9.*

Christ is a witness. He was a sworn witness when he gave testimony among the Jewish people that he was the "Amen" and "Yes" to all the testimonies or promises made of old to the fathers; indeed, that he was adjured by the Father. In order that he might testify to such, he had to be questioned and examined by the Jewish nation, which is here regarded entirely as a <term>court of law<note>original Hebrew: *Beit Din*, literally "House of Judgment."</note></term>, to which house God had left the examination of witnesses (*Deuteronomy 13:1-3 and 19:22*). He who is not ignorant of the customs and manners of the ancients will notice that I have had in mind the customs of the Hebrew people.

For we know that among them there was in use <term>inquiry<note>original Hebrew: *derishah*</note></term> and <term>investigation<note>original Hebrew: *chakirah*; Greek: *exetasis* and *anakrisis*</note></term>, or <term>testing<note>original Hebrew: *bedikah*; Greek: *exereunesis*</note></term>. Namely, they examined even the witnesses to see if they were <term>fit<note>original Hebrew: *kesherim*, meaning legally qualified witnesses.</note></term> and worthy, whose testimony would be accepted, or if they were <term>unfit<note>original Hebrew: *pesulim*, meaning disqualified from giving evidence.</note></term> to provide testimony. See *Tractate Sanhedrin, chapter 5*, and *Choshen Mishpat, Laws of Testimony*. And so every Israelite constituted a <term>court of law<note>original Hebrew: *Beit Din*</note></term>, and he is not obliged to grant belief to the testifying Christ before he has examined Christ, regarded as a witness. And that is the reason why Jesus, intending to give testimony among the Jews, was provided with such arguments that, when properly examined by the Jews, could convince them of the truth of his testimony. Christ himself brings forward these arguments (*John 5:33*): first John gave testimony regarding Christ as a known prophet; which was truly a <term>matter<note>original Hebrew: *davar*</note></term> or thing that contributed greatly to the <term>substance<note>original Hebrew: *le-inyan*</note></term> of the matter <term>in judgment<note>original Hebrew: *ba-din*</note></term>; for since John was the forerunner of the true Messiah, it was his primary duty to know who finally was the true Messiah who was to come into the world.

But Christ goes further, verse 36, and says: *“But I have a testimony greater than that of John. For the works which the Father has given me to finish, the very works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father has sent me.”* If you therefore do not believe the testimony of John, who is a man; well then, examine my works, which shall give testimony that I am the true witness.

He, Christ, goes further in verse 37: *“and the Father who has sent me, he himself testifies of me. You...”*

->AMEN. AMETHIST.<-
M 2

*and have never yet heard his voice, nor seen his form. Indeed, my father himself, whose voice you previously never heard, gave testimony of me at my baptism; and although he spoke to you of old on Mount Sinai, you demonstrate sufficiently by your example that you have long since forgotten his voice and form. But it was not him whose voice you heard, and whose majesty and glory you thereafter claim to have seen on the mountain, for John 1:18, no one has ever seen God, but this was the Angel of God, who spoke the living words, Acts 7:38. I, I am he himself, who in the name of my father, entered into and concluded a covenant with you at Horeb; yet you heard my father's voice and testimony at my baptism, and having noticed there are some among you who did not hear this voice, well then, see the voices and reasons of my father stand, contained in the holy scriptures, which were left to you by the prophets, verse 39. If you are therefore inclined to hear my speaking father, who grants testimony of me, search the scriptures <note>original: "onderzoekt de schriften"</note>, as you claim to do, for these testify of me.*

*Thus far I have wished to follow this excellent Lord, because his thoughts—being very learned, well-founded, and elaborate—belong singularly to my purpose.*

### AMETHYST, / <term>Achlamah<note>Hebrew: אחלמה</note></term> / <term>Amethystos<note>Greek: ἀμέθυστος, meaning "not drunken"</note></term> / Amethystus.

<margin>Variety of Amethysts.</margin>
THE AMETHYST is found once in the Old and once in the New Testament. *Exodus 28:19 and Revelation 21:20.*
Although it is the jeweler's craft to know and distinguish this noble stone, as with all others, I shall nonetheless not do wrong if I write concerning it that which writers before me—who hold name and esteem in the world of the learned—have testified of this stone: such as Pliny, Theophrastus, Agricola in *On Fossils* <note>original Latin: *de fossilibus*</note>, Epiphanius, Scaliger, Braun in *On the Clothing of the Hebrews* <note>original Latin: *de vestitu Ebræor.*</note> etc., from whom, as well as from Hofmann's *Universal Lexicon* <note>original Latin: *Lex. universale*</note>, I believe I have noted that amethysts differ from one another in colors, luster <note>original: "wateringen," referring to the clarity or "water" of a gem</note>, and otherwise; because of this, one is more praiseworthy than the other, though they are considered to be among the most prominent when their luster tends toward and draws near to the violet color, the color of red wine, rose-red, and light purple.

<margin>Testimonies of the learned.</margin>
The testimonies of the learned bring word that one finds this stone in India, Arabia, Armenia, Galatia, Cyprus, Tarsus, etc., and that, though one might find it elsewhere, it is nonetheless not as virtuous and praiseworthy as those from the aforementioned places.

<margin>Hebrew name.</margin>
As for the Hebrew name אחלמה *Achlamah*, I have noted that Abrabanel derives it from חלם *chalam*, "to dream," and that Aben Ezra is also at home there, bringing forward this reason: because it provokes many kinds of dreams in the wearer. Yet I consider that saying to be "sleepy thinking" <note>A pun on the word for dreaming</note> and dreaming in a serious matter. Others have derived the noun of this stone from *chalam*: "He was brave and strong"; having been weakened, he rose up again and received new strength. But that this stone should add singular strength to its wearer, and so restore fallen powers,

<column-break/>

that one who had been bedridden would, through the same, obtain such lasting strength that they would rise from the bed as if with fresh youth, can as yet find no belief or agreement from me.
<margin>Its powers called into doubt.</margin>

In Greek, this stone is called *Amethystos* <note>ἀμέθυστος</note>, *not fully intoxicated or drunk*: conversely, in this sense, sober, very well-composed of mind. But that this stone—through its emanations and influences in and upon the wearer—could bring it about that one never becomes intoxicated or drunk while using wine or other intoxicating drinks in abundance, is something I cannot only not fathom believing, but I say: it is particularly good that there are few such stones, and that they can only be obtained for a heavy price; otherwise, the children of Bacchus <note>A classical reference to heavy drinkers or followers of the wine god</note>, the heroes in drink, would multiply too greatly in number. For certainly, they are better off for whom moderation serves as an amethyst.

That this stone, the *Achlamah* or amethyst, stood as a representation of one of the twelve tribes of Israel on the High Priest’s breastplate, I do not think or expect anyone will persist in denying; it might come down to the choice of the tribes, either for Issachar or for Naphtali.

For my part, I shall view this amethyst stone as a symbolic means for Naphtali’s tribe: regarding whom I read in *Genesis 49:21* as follows: *Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words.* I have said that *Achlama* comes from *chalam*, to be brave and strong, to obtain new strength. It has a certain sweetness and spirited charm to it, that exactly this symbolic and memorial stone was suited to Naphtali’s tribe: for observe what Rachel poured out when her husband (Jacob) had fathered this Naphtali by her maidservant or chambermaid (Bilha), *Genesis 30:7, 8.* And Bilha, Rachel’s maidservant, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son. Then Rachel said, *with great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.*
<margin>Naphtali's tribe represented by it.</margin>

Rachel, Jacob’s wife, having been barren until that time, and Leah her sister, by contrast, having fathered several children by Jacob, this was a very great and heavy cross to Rachel. While she yet sought and desired offspring (*Genesis 30*), she assigned her maidservant (Bilha) to her husband (Jacob), by which Bilha he won more children than by Leah; this gave Rachel no small amount of pleasure, priding herself in seeing the family built up more strongly through her maidservant than through Leah her sister.

Which odd case, though rare, shall be little praised or followed.

Yet there is still something to say regarding Naphtali and the memorial and symbolic stone, the amethyst, based on *Genesis 49:21*, for I see that the translation brings this reading: *Naphtali is a hind let loose: he giveth goodly words.* Yet to me, this translation seems very appropriate and timely: *Naphtali is a hind let loose, or with repetition of the word Hind, a hind of him who gives good words.* It is a prophecy and prophetic tribal blessing from father Jacob, announcing to each tribe its future state, lot, and portion beforehand.

### AMETHYST.

Naphtali was situated and inherited land near the sea, in a secluded and far-distant corner of Galilee. The Jewish clergy, it seems, concerned themselves little with the Galileans; consequently, in matters of church and spiritual care—being so far removed from Jerusalem for instruction, strengthening, and words of comfort—they sat as if in a darkness, thirsty, and nearly faint <note>original: "amegtig," a wordplay on "Amethyst" suggesting one who is breathless or weary</note>.

Yet these people, belonging to the Israel of God, received from their father’s mouth this pleasant prophecy: that although they might be despised and neglected by the Jewish clergy for a time, they would remain the flock of Him who gives "beautiful words" *Isaiah 52:7.* They would one day hear very beautiful, living, and precious words and reasons, by which their thirsty hearts would be refreshed, strengthened, and wonderfully comforted and gladdened, just as it later came to pass: compare *Isaiah 8:23* and *9:2* with *Matthew 4:15, 16.*

<margin>Representation of Christ’s church.</margin>
And just as it happened with the literal Naphtali in early times, so has the portion of Christ’s church in a later joint of time been represented by Naphtali. This church has also wrestled the wrestlings of God <note>Naphtali's name means "my wrestling"</note>; she was shamefully neglected by the Roman clergy; she did not wish to become drunk on the wine of Babylon; she yearned for the pure waters of God’s Word and unadulterated instruction. And after the church had come out of Babylon by means of the Reformation and the breaking through of the suppressed and powerfully withheld light of the Gospel, she had to wrestle the wrestlings of God in no small measure. Thus, like the amethyst, she reflected the color of red wine through the heavy and bitter persecutions for the sake of religion in Spain, France, Piedmont, Hungary, Bohemia, Silesia, the Spanish Netherlands, etc.

<margin>Amethyst among the twelve foundation stones.</margin>
One finds, as already noted from *Revelation 21:20,* the amethyst stone among the twelve foundation stones. I know that Jesus is properly, emphatically, and alone in power the foundation of the church of God and the city of the church. *1 Corinthians 3:11.* <note>The original cites 2 Kor. III. 11, likely a scribal error for 1 Cor 3:11</note> I am also of the opinion that all the virtues and natural, laudable qualities of those twelve stones, both individually and taken together, are symbolic means of representing Him who is the foundation of the church—His prehistoric virtues, etc. Therefore, I consider it not entirely unhelpful to spiritualize what the amethyst truly (or even by common report) possesses in its nature. I shall show how the luster and glory of excellent and divine virtues, attributes, powers, and workings reveal themselves in the most excellent amethyst. When I apply this to Christ as the most excellent cornerstone and foundation stone, I assume that all twelve stones are intended—through their beautiful rays, worthiness, and otherwise—to collectively represent Him in His constancy, majesty, preciousness, power of bearing, support, glorification, and adornment. Consequently, I say that something common and something particular is found in all stones and in each of these stones.

<margin>Application of its colors and lusters.</margin>
As for the amethyst stones, they do not all have the same color and "water" <note>the clarity or luster of a gemstone</note>. However, noting some colors and lusters in these, I shall apply them to Christ by way of spiritualization.

If one attributes to amethyst stones a wine-white, <column-break/> pure luster: let it be so. Indeed, in Christ, the divine Book of the Bible teaches us that in Him—as God, as God-man, as becoming man, as being made under the Law, and in His nature, life, inner thoughts, passions, and deeds—the most perfect holiness and purity has appeared, which could be proven point by point.

If it is said that in the amethyst stones a hyacinth-violet heavenly color is found, let it be so.

It should suffer no contradiction that it be said, believed, and confessed of Christ—in truth and in emphatic power—that everything heavenly and tending toward heaven is found in Him; such as:

> a. His heavenly descent and birth, having God as a father and having descended from heaven.
> b. Close union and correspondence with the God of heaven: being the Father’s image and reflection; of one essence with the Father; having the name Jehovah in His inward part. *Exodus 23:21, John 1:1, 14,* and *10:30,* etc.
> c. Very close union with God, intimacy with His Father in prayers, addresses, thanksgivings, and otherwise. *Matthew 3:17* and *17:4, 5. John 12* and *17.*
> d. Entirely and completely heavenly in His will and intentions, as He willed what was the Father’s will, so that His will on earth perfectly agreed with the will of His Father in the heavens, for which His ears were also bored. <note>A reference to Psalm 40:6, symbolizing the servant's total obedience</note> *Psalm 40:7, 8, 9. Hebrews 10:5. John 4:34.*
> e. Just as He, who was the Lord of glory and descended from heaven, was afterwards taken up into heaven in glory. *John 3:13. Acts 1:9. 1 Timothy 3:16.*

If the rose-red, purple-fiery-red color is attributed in truth to the amethyst stones, let it be so.

I perceive in Christ—as Surety, Mediator, High Priest, God-Savior, Executor of the Father’s will for the radiance of the Father’s name and virtues, and for the redemption and liberation of His people—a blushing love, a glowing and burning zeal and earnestness. *Psalm 69:10. Song of Solomon 5:10.*

If one ascribes to the amethyst stones the red wine-color tending toward pale blue, as is sometimes seen in bruised or pinched stripes of flesh, spots, and skin blemishes: I have nothing against it.

Regarding Christ, as described in the Gospel scripture and painted to the life for us in His ignominious suffering, we can vividly represent such colors, lusters, and appearances to ourselves when we properly remember His bitter suffering and death. To this end, it can help much that we walk with Him to Gethsemane; return to the city and observe His mistreatment by Annas, Caiaphas, and Herod; and in the Pagan court before Pilate, having beheld Him with a woven crown of thorns and with nails through His hands and feet, hammered to the cursed cross-beam.

I would not dare to say with certainty, as I noted at the beginning, that the amethyst stone protects its wearer from drunkenness and keeps them sober; but I can say this with much more ground, and...

### AMETHYST.

and a stronger assurance regarding the power and the influence of the most excellent amethyst, Jesus, must testify that by being carried upon the breast through faith in the heart and through constant remembrance and earnest meditation, He keeps the wearer and possessor in a state not only of bodily, but also of spiritual sobriety of soul. *Romans 13:12, 13, 14; Luke 21:34; Ephesians 5:18.* Such a person shall not have their heart occupied and burdened with spiritual drunkenness, or by a love for the world and excessive care for the flesh; and because he seeks and pursues something more excellent, and knows that his soul’s adversary <note>referring to the Devil</note> seeks to outwit him, he is always on his guard. *Matthew 6:31, 32, 33, 34; 1 Peter 5:7, 8.*

Whether it be subsequently true or not that the amethyst stone makes the wearer brave, strong, and very encouraged to enter into battle:

<margin>Christ compared to an Amethyst.</margin>
It is certain that Christ, whom we now compare to an amethyst, makes those in whom He dwells through faith—*Ephesians 3:17*—and between whose breasts He rests like a bundle of myrrh—*Song of Solomon 1:13*—wonderfully courageous. He grants power and strength for the spiritual struggle, supports them, and makes all things possible for victory. *Matthew 16:18; 2 Corinthians 12:9, 10; Philippians 4:13; Romans 7:24, 25; 1 Corinthians 15:55, 56, 57; 1 John 5:4, 5; etc.*

When I represent to myself that the amethyst stone appears as the last stone among the foundation stones of the new, holy Jerusalem descended from heaven—*Revelation 21:20* <note>The text cites Acts 21:20, likely a printer's error for Revelation 21:20</note>—and if I may, in a certain but lesser symbolic power, compare the Apostles to foundation stones: then it seems to me that I could be mindful of the Apostle Matthias, who came to the Apostleship by lot in place of Judas Iscariot. *Acts 1:21, 22.* A very capable and godly man, known closely to the other Apostles of Jesus Christ, who had lived and associated with Jesus from the beginning until the end.

<margin>Also the Apostle Matthias.</margin>
In this Apostle, that which is said of the amethyst shone forth in many parts: of whom I shall briefly note here what can be found more extensively in the writings of Eusebius, Clement of Alexandria, Joachim Camerarius, Baudartius, Cave, and others.

Baudartius, in his *Memorable Sayings*, page 8, relates concerning the Apostle Matthias that he was often accustomed to say: *Everyone must constantly wage war with his own flesh, and keep the same in check, without allowing himself to follow his own lusts: if such occurs, then the soul shall grow and increase in faith and in knowledge, etc.* And such corresponds wonderfully with the useful and similar lessons and admonitions of the Apostle Paul. *1 Corinthians 9:24, etc.; Galatians 5:24; Ephesians 4:22, 23, 24, 25; Colossians 3:5, etc.*

The short course of his apostolic ministry, according to church historians, mostly amounts to this:

That he spent the first fruits of his service in Judea among the Jews, his own people; that he subsequently traveled eastward to preach and arrived in Cappadocia; and that

<margin>Cappadocians, a wild people.</margin>
because the Cappadocians were a wild, fierce people, he found much work to do in planting among them sobriety and the foundations of the Christian faith. When he had overcome these difficulties in many people, he encountered satanic men by

<column-break/>

whom he was miserably put to death. As to what kind of death Matthias died, or how they specifically dealt with him, I do not find the greatest agreement: for some believe that this Apostle was crucified, while others believe he was first stoned and afterwards beheaded.

When we then believe of Matthias that as a believer and a righteous man he shall never be moved—*Proverbs 10:30*—that he was a living and precious stone—*1 Peter 2:4, 5*;

That he was chosen as an Apostle in a lawful manner—*Acts 1:21*;

That he, along with the other Apostles, helped to lay the foundation—*Ephesians 2:20, 21*; that some among the Apostles were considered to be pillars—*Galatians 2:9*; and that he was not only a witness of the mouth but also a witness of blood <note>a martyr</note>, then we may lawfully conclude that he may have been represented by the amethyst stone.

But it seems to me that I shall do my godly Reader no disservice if, in spiritualizing the amethyst, I go on to show how every Christian must strive to become a Christian amethyst stone: employing all suitable means toward that end, and subsequently demonstrating and making such manifest in deed.

a. The violet sky-color observed in the amethyst stone serves as a symbol of the heavenly-mindedness of the children of God, who, not being conformed to this world—*Romans 12:2*—do not love the world. *1 John 2:16.* It is true that they do not exactly kick away worldly things with their feet when they flow to them lawfully; yet they do not seek and pursue them first and above all, but rather seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness. *Matthew 6:33.* They do not become proud of it, nor do they set their heart on increasing wealth. *Psalm 62:10.* But they seek the things above. *Colossians 3:1.* They reflect and understand that worldly, earthly goods can neither benefit their soul, nor improve it, nor buy it back from destruction. They find temporal treasures and powers to often be the swill <note>original: "draf," the waste from brewing or animal feed</note> of those whose portion is in this life, who in the divine scriptures are compared to dogs, wolves, bears, lions, tigers, and swine: that the world and what is in it is passing and perishable. *Matthew 6:20; 1 Corinthians 7:31.* Therefore, they do not desire to sell heaven for this common swill and this mess of pottage <note>original: "moesschotel," a reference to Esau's bowl of lentils</note>: they consider that they brought nothing into the world, and they shall carry nothing out of it.

<margin>The Pious compared to the Amethyst.</margin>
Therefore, they demonstrate their amethyst-like sky-color and form through their heavenly-mindedness, thoughts, and conduct, both before God and men: they sigh for and look toward the heavenly and divine. *Psalm 42:1 and 37; 2 Corinthians 5:2, 3, 4; Philippians 1:21, 23.*

Consequently, they immediately unite and join themselves with their hearts to the travelers toward heaven. *Psalm 16:3; Psalm 119:63; Proverbs 5:24.*

Therefore, they distinguish themselves through all their actions from the people of this world, whose portion is in this life: they behave as guests and strangers: they walk the paths which lead them directly to heaven, of faith, love, hope, holiness, godliness, etc.

# AMETHYST.

The amethyst represents the holy blush, shame, and embarrassment of true Christians. Rebekah, when she saw Isaac from afar, was covered with a blush and covered herself with her veil, *Genesis 24:65.* Redness suddenly falling upon a fair countenance is a sign of shame; therefore, "shame-redness" <note>A literal translation of the Dutch *schaamrootheit*, referring to the deep red blush of modesty or repentance.</note> is mentioned in Holy Scripture, *Ezra 9:6 <note>The OCR reads Ezra 7, but the context of blushing for sin points to Ezra 9:6.</note>, Isaiah 3:9,* and is regarded as something virtuous. Conversely, not knowing how to turn pale or blush, and not being ashamed or becoming "shame-red," is a sign of having a bold, unfeeling, shameless, and hard heart. *Isaiah 1:12; Jeremiah 3:3 and 6:15; Zephaniah 3:5; etc.*

For although the children of God have been made free through the Son and have much boldness before God, yet in this earthly state, being far lower than the angels and seraphim, infinitely below God, and still beset with many sins and imperfections, they have reason to cover themselves, to be ashamed, and to blush.

Besides this rose-red color of shame, there is in and among the children of God a fiery amethyst color of love for God and for one's neighbor—for the honor of God, for the keeping of His commandments, and for the edification and salvation of one's neighbor—which shines through their eyes, upon their lips, and in all their conduct. To demonstrate what stirs the children of God to this: *a.* in regard to the Triune God; *b.* in regard to the Son of God, considered in His nature, offices, states, virtues, works, and blessings; *c.* the commandments of God in themselves and in their consequences; *d.* their fellow men, especially their fellow brothers and sisters, etc.—to show all this would require too much complexity in this work of mine; therefore, one may consult those authors who have written on Christian virtues and moral duties.

<margin>
*b.*
</margin>
Regarding the red wine-color found in the amethyst stone; I shall say little of how this is found among true Christians, the true members of the body of Jesus Christ. Yet this also occurs in them, insofar as they participate through faith in Him, in His death and His suffering on the cross, *Romans 6:7.* However, those who experience times of refreshing and peace have weighty reason to kindle for God the incense of heartfelt thanksgiving; and those who act prudently prepare themselves against the day of evil and against the heat of oppression.

<margin>
*d.*
</margin>
And assuming it were true that the amethyst stone induced sleep in the wearer; in a different respect, the amethyst Jesus induces in His own both waking and sleeping; and in this, the teachers—primarily as the foundational builders of the New Jerusalem—follow their Lord, Head, and Master. And so does every member of Jesus Christ.

While many snore in an unfeeling sleep of sin and carelessness, lying open to all kinds of danger (which is usually joined with the eternal sleep), no upright Christian or Christian teacher sleeps there; rather, they wake and watch over themselves and the congregations, which is why teachers, by virtue of their office, are also called "seers" and "watchmen." They cry out: *Awake, you who sleep, arise from the dead, and Christ shall give you light. Ephesians 5:14.*

<column-break/>

Yet, a kind of sleep is produced in them, consisting of a holy trust in God, a quiet rest in the Lord, a lying down and sleeping in a divine manner under His faithful, powerful, and fatherly governance and care for them, being certain that nothing shall harm them. *Psalm 3:6 and 4:9.*

<margin>
*e.*
</margin>
If it be that the amethyst stone keeps the senses sober <note>The name "amethyst" comes from the Greek *a-methystos*, meaning "not drunken," based on the ancient belief that the stone protected its wearer from intoxication.</note>; a child of God has this power of grace from God within himself. As much as he is able to influence others through earnest exhortations and an example of sobriety, he does not neglect to put into practice whatever else may serve Christian moderation. To this end, he reminds himself and his neighbor that the creature <note>Meaning created things, such as food or wine.</note>, when used in excess to the bewilderment of the mind and judgment, causes one to forget God the benefactor, *Deuteronomy 32:6-15;* that one transforms oneself into a beast in that manner and adopts all kinds of improper customs and unseemly behaviors. *Isaiah 28:7, 8.* The Lacedaemonians <note>The ancient Spartans.</note>, to frighten their children away from beastly drinking and foul gluttony, used to make their slaves drunk, so that the children, seeing the buffoonery, foolish clamor, and expressions of these men, and hearing their slurred speech, might develop an aversion to it. Drunkenness is the womb of many evils, *Proverbs 23:29, 30, 31, etc.;* drunkenness is a form of idolatry, for it so charms a person that they cannot keep themselves from becoming a total slave to the creature and to their lusts; revelry and drunkenness cause a person's state to end in deep poverty, *Proverbs 21 and 23.* Diogenes, seeing the house of a drunkard up for sale, said: *I always thought that he would eventually vomit up his house as well.* Thus, drunkards not only lie exposed to many dangers, wasting their health, life-force, and temporal means, and miserably misusing God’s creatures, but they also lie exposed to eternal disgrace. *1 Corinthians 6:10; Galatians 5:19, 20, 21.*

<margin>
*f.*
</margin>
And so that the righteous might awaken and increase the power of the amethyst's strengthening, both in themselves and in their neighbor, they themselves take refuge—and teach others to do the same—in divine grace, with prayers and tears, and in the use of spiritual weapons, *2 Corinthians 10:4, 5; Ephesians 6:12, 13, etc.;* so that they must never rely on themselves, on their own understanding and strength, or on the arm of the flesh, but only on the living God. They frequently use these words of exhortation: *Psalm 27:14, Wait on the Lord, be strong, and He shall strengthen your heart; yes, wait on the Lord. Psalm 31:25, Be strong, and He shall strengthen your heart, all you who hope in the Lord.*

# AMETHYST. AMIA. AMIANTUS.

one is satiated after a sorrowful and very difficult panting and longing, and endowed in the later days with an inheritance of the lands westward toward the sea, and southward toward the islands; formerly the Gospel first rose in the east and broke through to the west, and from there moved through to the cold and deep north. It may well be expected that the light of the Gospel shall move and penetrate toward America and other western coasts, southward through Africa to its original place. *Psalm 68:28, 29. <margin>Another observation.</margin>
Furthermore, I have also this observation to present in all modesty, should there be anyone who would prefer to see the amethyst stone applied to another Apostle rather than to Matthias.

It is such that the amethyst stone appears as the last in the representation in *Revelation 21:20*, and that in *Acts 1*, James the Less <note>Also known as James, son of Alphaeus.</note> appears in the Apostolic rank as the ninth, which Apostle, according to *Galatians 2:8, 9*, along with Cephas <note>Peter</note> and John, was considered a pillar: and he seems to have presided over the Council at Jerusalem, *Acts 15*. He is held to have been the overseer or bishop of Christ's congregation there; a man of singular zeal and modesty, very pious and excellent in life and conduct; yet he met a wretched end. With the salvation of all Israel, the Lord can first truly be said to have laid the last amethyst foundation stone to that glorious church-city, that New Jerusalem descended from heaven.

# AMIA, a fish.

I find this fish named by Fransius as a *Welfz* <note>Likely referring to a species of the Scombridae family, such as a bonito or small tunny.</note>. It is suggested, likely not without reason, that it is named AMIA from the privative *alpha* and *mia* <note>original: "ex alpha pr. troct. & mia"</note>, meaning not one or alone, but swimming together in entire schools; being a sea fish which also stays in great numbers in the rivers and multiplies greatly; having curved teeth like saws, of which it is very proud, although otherwise it has somewhat limp and weak flesh. One may read of this in Pliny, Book 9, Chapter 16.

These fish join together against sea monsters, while encircling the smaller species to try and place them in greater safety. One may read of this in Pliny, Book 9, Chapter 16.

I have not found this fish described more closely; and I can not unfittingly regard it in its companionship and mutual activity for common protection as a symbol of how small things and powers are formidable and expand when they help and assist one another. "Harmony makes small things grow; united strength is stronger" <note>original: "Concordia res parvae crescunt vis unita fortior"</note>: unity makes might.

<margin>Power of unity.</margin>
For which reason Horace, praising the harmony of spouses in the 13th Song of the first book, rightly said:

> *Thrice happy and more are those*
> *Whom an unbroken bond holds, and whom no love,*
> *Torn asunder by evil complaints,*
> *Will release sooner than their final day.*
<note>original: "Felices ter & amplius, / Quos irrupta tenet copula nec malis / Divulsus querimoniis / Suprema citius solvet amor die."</note>

->That is:<-

> *Happy are they, whom firm marriage-faith*
> *Binds; then man and wife live*
> *In sturdy harmony, which death alone can break.*

And Publius:

> *Discord makes harmony more precious.*
> *Humble aids are made firm by consensus.*
<note>original: "Discordia fit carior concordia. / Auxilia humilia, firma consensus facit."</note>

->That is:<-

> *He who has tasted discord finds the true value*
> *Of harmony, which binds and strengthens all on earth.*
> *A small help also becomes firm and strong through unity.*

# AMIANTUS, Amiant or Shimmer-stone.

I have read here and there of the province of Chinchintalas <note>A region in Tartary/China mentioned by Marco Polo.</note> in China, and that there is a certain mountain where one finds minerals mixed with some earth-substances, which are quite thread-like and very woolly: that after drying this substance in the sun's rays, one pounds and strikes it in a metal mortar, and by so doing, cleanses it of the earthy parts, after which one can weave linen garments from it once it is spun; which linen or woolly garments, when they are soiled, are thrown into the fire and purified.

<margin>Clothes purified in the fire.</margin>
In leafing through some writers, I have noticed that the ancients called this substance *asbestus*.

However, I found in no small number of famous writers that AMIANTUS is a shaggy, tufted, woolly stone: soft, somewhat weak, whitish, and pulling slightly toward green: being a stone that can be cleaved and split, whose body consists of closely adhering threads: somewhat shaggy and woolly, especially when rubbed. It is said that one can spin threads from it and weave and prepare clothes, towels, etc., which do not melt in the fire, but whose soiling is entirely removed by the fire: of which stone it is said that it wards off and renders powerless both poisoning and the power of enchantment.

One reads of it in Pliny *page (in my edition) 720*; De Mey *Physiological Meditations, part 2, page 114*; etc. Jonston *page 44*; Venerus Martinus Martinii; Kircher in *The Subterranean World*; etc. Braunius *On the Clothing of the Hebrews, page 135*.

Lamp wicks are made from it, as they are not consumed by the flame of the fire.

Caussinus cites Basil, applying the amiantus stone to the three youths who came unharmed out of Babylon’s very hotly stoked furnace <note>A reference to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the Book of Daniel.</note>.

The same writer cites Jerome, applying this to chastity, which loses nothing in the heat of impure love, and powerfully resists the fire of flattery and poisoning.

# AMIANTUS. AMMON.

<margin>Chastity compared to the glimmer-stone.</margin>
*Chastity is compared to this stone <note>Amiantus, or asbestos, known for its fire-resistance</note>, which is not wounded by the fire of desire, much less consumed; indeed, it is not even tarnished by the rust of evil inclinations or smoke, but holds the upper hand in the trial, and always comes to light shining, adding an arrow of innocence and a stainless conscience.*

Augustine, *On Definitions*: "Chastity is a pure and honorable condition of the whole body, achieved by taming the furies of vice." <note>original Latin: "Castitas est per edomitas vitiorum furias munda, & honesta totius corporis habituda"</note>

Augustine, *The City of God*, Book 1, Chapter 22: *Chastity cannot be violated by force, neither in the body nor in the soul.*

One could apply the amiantus to many other things, which I will not busy myself with now, except that I will set down one more reflection: namely, that no amiantus stone is so precious for many uses, or as durable, as a faithful and holy child of God—even if they are weak in themselves, soft, and woven together from thready flesh and sinews. *Job 10:10, 11.*

Nevertheless, such a person has this in common with the amiantus stone: not only that they do not perish through the fire of the cross <note>referring to trials and suffering</note>, but even that they are refined and purified of the stains of sin and defects by it, so that they come out of the fire all the more brightly. *Psalm 66:10. Zechariah 13:9. Malachi 3:1, 2, 3. Psalm 119:71. Hebrews 12:11. James 1. Psalm 94:12.*

### AMMON, AMMONITES,
### עמונים / עמון <note>Hebrew: Ammonim / Ammon</note>

<margin>Genesis 9.</margin>
In the holy scroll, Genesis 9, one reads of Ham or Canaan; some believe he was named Hammon, Ham, or Am, from which comes Jupiter Ammon <note>A syncretic deity blending the Greek Zeus/Jupiter with the Egyptian Amun</note>, either from *chajim* <note>Hebrew: "hot"</note> meaning "to be hot," or from *ammos* <note>Greek: "sand"</note> meaning "sand," found in the Libyan hot, dry, and sandy region. Catullus writes:

->*The oracle of Jove amidst the sweltering heat.*<-
<note>original Latin: "Oraclum Jovis inter æstuosi"</note>

->That is:<-

->*In the sand where Jupiter gives his church-oracles.*<-

Propertius:

->*Neither would this unfold the sandy cave of Libyan Jove.*<-
<note>original Latin: "Hec neque arenosum libyci Jovis explicet antrum"</note>

->That is:<-

->*This would not reveal to us*<-
->*The oracle of the Libyan Jupyn <note>Jupiter</note>.*<-

See Bochart in the chapter on Peleg, Micraelius, Kipping, Curtius's *History* book 4, Pomponius Mela book 1, Justin book 1.

It is held by some that this was Menes <note>The first Pharaoh of Egypt</note>, who, having moved to Egypt, took possession of that land and built Memphis there; and having been elevated to the number of the gods by his people, he was honored. At least, one reads of Ammon, and of a city and places belonging to him. *Psalm 78, 105, and 106. Jeremiah 46:25. Ezekiel 30:15. Read Marsham's Chronological Canon, pages 23, 30, 26, 28.*

However all this may be, Holy Scripture does not point us toward this Ammon, but toward someone else as the father of the Ammonites (Genesis 19:30): namely, to the son whom Lot fathered in incest with his younger daughter.

<column-break/>

<margin>Origin of the Ammonites.</margin>
From him are descended those peoples called the children of Ammon, living in the region of Rephaim, between the Syrians and the Moabites. The Lord did not want Israel to mix with them or to wage war against them—that is, to initiate war or take their land by arms—for they were descended from Lot, Abraham's nephew, and thus were of kin; the Lord had given them that land. *Deuteronomy 2; 2 Chronicles 20; Deuteronomy 23:3, 6; Nehemiah 13; Ezra 9.* They were very idolatrous and honored Milcom and Moloch. *1 Chronicles 11 and 2 Chronicles 23.*

This people, however, joined with other Canaanites and was very hostile to Israel, and they waged war against them more than once. Jephthah, Saul, and David beat and "clipped their wings" quite a bit, and they were made tributary to Israel. *2 Chronicles 27.*

It is true that the king of the Ammonites complained (Judges 11:13) that Israel had taken away his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, which seemed to conflict with Deuteronomy 2. But one must know that the children of Israel took it not from them, but from the Amorites, who had won it by arms (Deuteronomy 3; Numbers 21; Joshua 5). They took it through a lawful war against the Amorites, and therefore they had not taken it from the Ammonites. The Spirit of God records the king's claim, but does not decide whether it was truth or a lie; He leaves it undetermined and in the middle.

The Lord threatened the Ammonites with heavy judgments, and one reads remarkable prophecies concerning them. *Jeremiah 9:26, 25, and 49. Amos 1. Isaiah 11:14. Ezekiel 25. Zephaniah 2.*

One reads in Isaiah 11 that the children of Ammon shall be obedient to them <note>Israel</note>, and they shall lay their hands upon Edom and Moab. This is true insofar as they made them tributary and bound them to servant-like submission (2 Chronicles 27; 2 Samuel 8:14; Deuteronomy 23:7). Or, one might wish to understand this as signifying that the church in the last days shall enlighten, convert, and make these ignorant and idolatrous heathens subject to Christ's scepter. Or, that the church in the last days would strive to bring those of the Roman faith—living in spiritual Edom, Moab, and Ammon, by whom she was constantly besieged—to the soul-and-manner-sanctifying knowledge of God in the face of Christ.

It is certain that the Antichristian beast, which in the company of others assaults the church from all sides (Revelation 16:12, 16 and 20:9), following the example of the enemies in Psalm 83:7, 8, 9, shall find itself robbed of its power and dominion, and that all kingdoms shall be given to the holy people. *Daniel 2 and 7. Zechariah 14:9. Isaiah 60:12.*

In general, one can observe that the inheritance of the Israel of God in the New Testament—namely, the world—is not fully obtained or possessed without much and violent opposition from many kinds of peoples who occupy a major part of the world. Among these are some who are somewhat our kin <note>meaning they share a common religious or historical root</note>, as if descended from Lot, Abraham's nephew; yet they have become idolatrous and unbelieving, and hostile toward the true believers, joining with heathen and entirely idolatrous peoples to resist and suppress the true Israel of God, and to halt the progress of the Lord’s people.

# AMNON, אמנון <note>Hebrew: Amnon</note>.

<margin>Meaning of AMNON.</margin>
AMNON is said to mean *faithful, truthful, a foster-child, or son of his mother*.

He was David’s son, and indeed his firstborn, as is judged, sired by Ahinoam; whose name is said to mean *the brother’s beauty and delight, a brother of movement*. This AMNON was very strongly in love with his half-sister Tamar. Feigning to be ill, he desired to be served by her, so that she might prepare tasty food for him. While she was performing this in his chamber and bringing the food to his bed, she was seized by him with force and violated; after which she was hated by him quite as strongly as she had previously been loved; so much so that he rejected her and had her shamefully cast out of the house; which disgrace he had to pay for with death more than two years later, through Absalom’s plot. *1 Samuel 14 and 25. 1 Chronicles 3. 2 Samuel 13. etc.* <note>The author cites 1 Samuel 14 and 25, though the primary narrative of Amnon is in 2 Samuel 13.</note>

<margin>The rape of Tamar.</margin>
<margin>Amnon killed by Absalom.</margin>
<margin>Meaning of Tamar.</margin>
Tamar, it is said, means *a palm tree, the fruit of that tree, a finger, exchange, and bitterness*.

<margin>The harmfulness of unchastity.</margin>
Carnal lust and lewdness are deadly. They make the body weak; they are a fountain of incurable ailments. Diogenes was not wrong when he said: *The interest paid on pleasure is death* <note>original Latin: "Voluptatis usura mors est"</note>. Burning lust usually takes its leave with deadly and chilly cold; for it quickly squanders the heat and flames, and is turned into loathing and hatred.

When the soul couples itself through burning desire with many things, and has run its course in sinful enjoyment—such as the pride of the eyes, the lust of the flesh, etc.—it finds, though often too late, that all is vanity; indeed, that in laughter her sorrow is born, and the end is but grief, *Proverbs 14:13. Ecclesiastes 2:1, 2.* and that the master of death, in the midst of joy, brings such a person to death, it being the wages of sin, *Romans 6:21-23.* for which one must be ashamed.

<margin>Amnon lives again in the Popes.</margin>
Certainly, one finds Amnon living again in many Popes; indeed, they are even more foul in all kinds of impurity, incest, and rape. Out of very many, I shall provide a very few examples.

<margin>John XIII.</margin>
John XIII of that name was a surrendered scoundrel.

Platina, in the *Lives of the Popes*, testifies of him that *he was a monster among men; that from his youth he was occupied with all kinds of filthiness and foul defects; more inclined to hunting and hawking—which was somewhat hindered by his immoderate lifestyle—than to prayer; that he was the foulest and most villainous of all Popes*. And Liutprand of Cremona testifies of him: *That he defiled himself with all kinds of filth, adultery, incest, dicing, gaming, and the pursuit of Venus <note>Meaning sexual obsession</note>, in which he called upon the evil spirit for help; drank wine to his loves, and in his carnal embrace was struck dead by the devil*. Of Pope Paul III, Sixtus IV and V, Alexander VI, etc., there would be a great deal to say. In their *Taxa Pænitentiariâ* <note>A list of fees for the absolution of various sins</note>, printed in Paris in the year 1520, one reads: 1. *A layman who has committed incest gives four turnoyzen.* <note>Turnoyzen refers to the "Gros Tournois," a silver coin of Tours.</note> 2. *One who has committed adultery and incest gives six turnoyzen.* 3. *An adulterer with his concubine together, six turnoyzen, two ducats.* 4. *A Clergyman who has committed sin with Nuns, inside or outside the Convent, or with his blood relatives, or with a spiritual daughter, or with any other foul sin, pays and atones ninety turnoyzen, twelve ducats, six Carlynen.* <note>Carlynen refers to the "Carlino," a small silver coin named after King Charles of Naples.</note>

# AMORITES, אמורי <note>Hebrew: Emori</note>.

<margin>Meaning of AMORITES.</margin>
AMORITES are descendants of Canaan’s son, *Genesis 10.* according to the property of the language meaning as much as *bitter ones, rebels, who have much talk and saying*: a great and mighty people, residing in the mountains. These, although they inhabited the high and strong places, yet being in no way satisfied with their dwelling place, came across the Jordan and possessed the kingdom from Arnon to Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan. They troubled the Moabites and Ammonites with war, taking away Bashan, Heshbon, and what lies between Arnon and Jabbok. *Deuteronomy 3. Numbers 5:21. Joshua 5. etc.*

<margin>A wild people.</margin>
A people that was to be rooted out, *Genesis 15. Deuteronomy 20.* partly rooted out, partly made tributary, *Judges 1.* Their land was divided among the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh, *Numbers 11. Deuteronomy 2. Judges 11.* which was singularly a work of God, *Psalm 44. Psalm 90:9, 10. Psalm 135 and 136. Jeremiah 32. Ezekiel 20. Isaiah 28. Amos 1.* after the kings Sihon and Og were defeated.

Certainly, the Lord, in driving out these nations along with the rest, showed His faithfulness, bared His power and arm, glorified His name, and wished to pave the way for a much greater grace in His son, *Psalm 44:4. Psalm 136:17-22.* and the subsequent inheritance of the world; and to make the people of Israel love their covenant God all the more strongly, to cling to Him, and to be more diligently obedient. *Psalm 105:44, 45.*

<margin>Israel equated with them.</margin>
One reads that Israel is equated with the Heathen nations, and that they have their birth from Canaan, *Ezekiel 16.* which is truth in various respects: for so Judah married a Canaanite woman and fathered children by her, *Genesis 38.* and not only the spiritual but also the worldly in Israel took foreign Canaanite wives and fathered children by them. *Ezra 9 and 10.*

Before God took them as a people, they were like the Canaanites: indeed, being in the outward covenant with God, they made themselves like these nations in unbelief, godlessness, idolatry, and what is more, for which reason they were also conquered and scattered among the Japhetites <note>Referring to the descendants of Japheth, often identified as Europeans or Gentiles</note>.

Certainly, if any nation has swallowed up and brought down other nearby nations, it is the Roman power, which even overwhelmed the land of Palestine as an Edom. I know of no nation with which the early Christian church had more unrest and sorrow, after her struggle with the Jews and Jewish Christians, than with and from the Romans for three hundred years: and still a part remains in name and appearance, though not in power and glory, of the old Roman Empire, which leaves the church no rest.

<margin>The church disturbed by the Romans.</margin>
However, the church had Joseph's blessing and victory to that extent. It received an open door when it found itself singularly under Constantine the Great in Asia, Syria, Palestine, Egypt, Greece, France, Spain, Italy, and men...

# AMORITES. AMPHISBAENA. ANATHEMA.

yet no strife or schism between the Eastern and Western churches was heard of.

It is observed that this people, as the most numerous and powerful in Canaan, are taken to represent all inhabitants and enemies of Israel, with whom the people of the Lord had to struggle until the very end, representing, as it were, the seven nations of Canaan. We know how the Christian church, in the seven periods of the New Testament, has had and will have its enemies to a greater or lesser degree, and that they can all be categorized under the name of Antichrist, who set themselves against Christ. These appeared early on when claiming the inheritance of the world, especially in the East and West; however, they shall be finished and overcome both by divine judgments and by the sword of the Word, and be subjected to the King of the whole earth, especially toward that time when the kingdom of the Israel of the New Testament on earth shall come to an end.

Thus, all believers, while they are in the Canaan on earth, before they come to the full possession of <margin>The struggle of believers on earth.</margin> the Canaan that is above, have a constant and hostile struggle with wicked men, especially with their internal and external enemies; it being useful for them, as it once was for Israel—however difficult—to be in constant hand-to-hand combat with such enemies.

### AMPHISBAENA, or a two-headed Snake.

<margin>Two-headed snakes.</margin> To have two heads, specifically one at the front and one at the back—though then there is properly no "back"—is monstrous and not at all according to the common course of nature and procreation. However, I see that Nicander <note>A Greek poet and physician from the 2nd century BCE who wrote about venomous creatures.</note> has quite a few followers who have provided us with a description of a **TWO-HEADED SNAKE**, one where the head should be and one where the tail should be: for Aristotle, Pliny, Isidore, Solinus, Aldrovandus, Jonstonus, Franzius, Olaus Magnus, etc., make mention of it.

One cannot entirely deny that they exist, for nature does not always work according to fixed rules. One finds unusual things among animals; but one might wonder whether this snake—being almost equally thick and round everywhere, having such thick and bulging cheeks that one can hardly see the eyes, a thick and hard skin, and being, as they say, somewhat speckled—is not named as such because one could not well distinguish at which end the head stood; also because it moved forward in a curved manner with both head and tail, or almost as readily forward and backward, as more animals do, just as others go or creep sideways.

It is said that it is the first among the snakes to come out of its hole in the cold; that next to other snakes it makes a small opening through which it spreads the poison to all parts of the body.

Furthermore, we are told that whenever a <margin>Power attributed to the Amphisbaena.</margin> pregnant woman steps over this Amphisbaena, whether it be alive or even dead, her fruit will pass from her prematurely.

That this dead snake, deprived of its poison and placed upon the pulsing veins, stills pain; that Egyptian Coriander, taken internally or placed upon the bite, is good against the poison of this snake; and further such things of that nature, which I do not exactly believe too readily.

I am inclined to think that by the naming and description of this monster and misshapen animal, one

<column-break/>

could bring to mind such things that appear so crooked, backward, so dark and confused, that one can find, as the saying goes, neither head nor tail to them.

I am willing to believe that imagining this snake going backward according to the different placement of the heads, one could bring to mind how the devil, that old serpent, can not only turn himself in various coils like the crooked, devious snakes, but also display two different heads and faces. He shows himself as he is by his own nature, and then, as if against nature like a snake with a head where the tail should be, as an angel of light—which is entirely uncharacteristic of him. These two heads cannot well exist together on him if he is to have success in his designs, unless he makes wonderful coils and turns, and strangely mixes evil and good together, making cunning and malice his companions. He must do one for the sake of the other, in order to prick and poison the souls of men in one way or another, either from the front or the back. If he always worked with violence, he would have few disciples; he must also occasionally be able to give in through cunning.

It is well known that the snake was cited by our Savior as a symbol of prudence. Now this Amphisbaena, having two heads, front and back, can represent for us a wise and prudent man, who must look not only forward but also backward; seeking to see through the future and the past; bringing together and weighing the present and the past; considering what outcome and "tail" the matter might have, so that at all times—after he has found the matter to be advisable or inadvisable—he may undertake or cease, continue or abandon it halfway, being allowed to begin and proceed with the matter intelligently and with good result, or to abandon it in time and shrink back from his intention and the work he has begun. <margin>The Snake as a symbol of prudence.</margin>

This is especially required in a military commander, who must have a "head" to be able to lead his troops with good order both toward and away from the enemy. Just as this symbol is also applicable to all statesmen.

### ANATHEMA, *Anathema* <note>original Greek: ἀνάθεμα</note>.

I have noticed that some learned men have made a distinction between *Anathema* <note>original Greek: ἀνάθεμα</note> and *Anathema/Offering* <note>original Greek: ἀνάθημα</note>.

**ANATHEMA** is taken to mean that which is banned, consecrated to God, and by promise or divine determination and will, belonging to Him alone, whether it be appointed for service or to be destroyed and rooted out, which then could not be sold, alienated, or claimed and appropriated by anyone. One reads of this in *Leviticus 27:28, 29.*

As far as temporal goods and inanimate things were concerned, such as gold, silver, and copper, they had to be brought to the services of the Lord in the Tabernacle or Temple.

That which was of livestock or humans had to die. Thus in Jericho, everything that had life, except for Rahab, had to die; the city had to be burned and devastated; no one was allowed to lay hands on it to rebuild it; gold, silver, copper, etc., had to be for the Lord; no one was allowed to claim that for themselves, no one was allowed to spare the living, <margin>Destruction of Jericho.</margin>

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous page, transitioning from the symbolic enemies of Israel (the Amorites) and the monstrous Amphisbaena to a detailed exploration of the concept of 'Anathema'—the religious ban or curse. It connects biblical practices with Greek, Roman, and Druidic traditions of sacrifice and excommunication.</meta>

-># ANATHEMA.<-
->N 2<-

or to bring under one's power. *Joshua 6 and 7; Numbers 7; 1 Samuel 12; 2 Samuel 8; Leviticus 27:28, 29.*

<margin>Meaning of the word ANATHEMA.</margin>
The word *ἀνάθεμα* <note>original Greek: *anáthema*</note> ANATHEMA means *separated, torn away, estranged*. Suidas explains it in this manner: *τὸ εἰς ἀφανισμένον εἱόμενον* <note>original Greek: *to eis aphanisménon heirómenon*</note>, "that which is to be removed from the midst so that it is seen no more." This should not be understood in an unlimited sense: for inanimate things remained for the use of the Tabernacle and Temple service, insofar as they could have any use there for service, ornament, remembrance, etc.; however, they were removed from common sight and use, and sometimes hung up and set aside in the temple as ornaments, trophies, and joyful memorials. Otherwise, cattle and humans were not to be spared, *Joshua 6*; to spare or seize anything for oneself was taken very ill, *Joshua 7; 1 Samuel 15.* And certainly, the case of Jericho seems to have been very hard and severe; yet it occurred concerning great sinners worthy of death, and open enemies of God and his people, conquered not by Israel but by the Lord.

One also perceives some traces of this among the Heathens. For so Cicero tells us in *On the Agrarian Law, Speech 2*: regarding the destruction of Carthage, that *Scipio the African, following the opinion of his Council, consecrated this city, so that this place, which had contended with Rome for mastery, should show the remains of its misery.* And Zonaras says in volume 2: *She is so given over to curses, that no one was permitted to build her up again.* With some distinction, Appianus mentions the destruction of this city: *The city of Carthage being destroyed, the free looting and plundering was permitted to the soldiers, with the exception of gold, silver, and the gifts or things given to the Gods.* And thereafter: *And the remaining booty being sold, he, dressed in the fashion of his country, dedicated the shields, war gear, and useless ships to Mars and Minerva, and burnt them with fire.*

<margin>Destruction of Carthage.</margin>

<margin>A human called anathema.</margin>
I have also noted that a person was called *ἀνάθεμα* <note>original: *anáthema*</note>, or was considered worthy of being banished by God and men; a cursed head, or one upon whom all the sins, curses, and punishments of the people had to descend—namely, *homo sacer* <note>Latin: "a sacred man," meaning one devoted to a deity for sacrifice or punishment</note>, who had to atone for the common good: whether offering himself voluntarily for that purpose or being chosen.

<margin>Humans slaughtered for sacrifices.</margin>
Which singularly used to occur among many Heathens during common national plagues and judgments—in famine, pestilence, heavy mortality, times of dearth, and also in floods—namely, that they sacrificed humans to turn away the wrath of the Gods thereby.

The Greeks, says Suidas, called them *pharmacoï* <note>original: *pharmakoí*, meaning "remedies" or "scapegoats"</note>, who were maintained out of the common means, so that by their downfall they might reconcile the cities.

The Athenians slaughtered two men annually, one for the men and one for the women.

Whenever the people of Marseille were tormented with the pestilence, one of the poor people offered himself, who had to be maintained for an entire year out of the common means with the purest food.

The Carthaginians, according to the account of Justin, brought humans and even minors to the altar, praying for the favor of the Gods through their blood.

And so Lactantius relates of those of Carthage, that fearing the deity was offended, they sacrificed two hundred children of the nobles so that they might pay for a means of atonement.

<column-break/>

The famous Druids of the Franks <note>The author likely refers to the Gauls described by Caesar</note> excused this desecration by saying that the Divine being could not be reconciled regarding the life of a human unless one gave the life of a human to the deity. So Caesar testifies in the 6th book of the *Gallic Wars*.

Of the manifold *ananthemata*, bans, curses, and punishments among the Jews, along with their distinctions, I shall not speak here. I think that *Anathema* and *Maranatha* agree among the Jews to the extent that they signified the ultimate curse, estrangement, and cutting off from all civil and ecclesiastical fellowship, with a full handing over of someone to the Lord’s judgment and righteous vengeance, both here and hereafter.

It is in many respects a truth that the Jewish civil and ecclesiastical state, along with the unbelieving people, was righteously struck by God with an *anathema*, ban, or curse, through the banishment and destruction of the land, city, and sanctuary, which they have not been permitted or able to rebuild; just as they are still burdened with such an *anathema* to this day, *Hosea 1 and 2; Malachi 4; Matthew 11; 1 Thessalonians 2:16*, etc., according to the pattern of the Heathens, whose place they now fill in the New Testament.

It is also clear from experience that the Antichrist annually places the confessors of the pure truth under the ban, and subjects them to his *anathemata* and pronouncements of curses.

<margin>Confessors of the Antichrist banned.</margin>
But I believe that in the final state of Jesus' kingdom, these *anathemata* shall be no more; when not only the *anathemata* of the Antichrist shall be destroyed, turned into powerless lightning bolts, and found to be such; but also because of the general gathering and conversion, or the influx of Jews and Heathens, these *anathemata*, curses, and banishments, and the most sorrowful separations and estrangements, shall no longer be found. *Zechariah 14:11; Revelation 22:3.*

I wish here, on the occasion of the Heathen *ananthemata* or human sacrifices to the Gods to remove wrath and heavy judgments, to be mindful of the Son of God, the Christ, who as a surety lay under the curses of the Law and bore the curse of the law to redeem and set free the guilty. *Galatians 3:13; Zechariah 3:9.* And it was useful and necessary that one should die for the people, so that the whole nation should not perish, although the Jewish head <note>referring to the High Priest Caiaphas</note> very likely did not mean or understand it so when speaking thus.

Paul, if he could turn away the judgment of his brothers that was approaching, would even wish to be an *anathema*, a banishment from Christ, *Romans 9*; not that he hated Jesus, himself, or his own salvation (for he knew that the love of God in Christ was unbreakable), but if it could please God, if it could be so, and all Israel through his banishment from Christ could obtain a share in the Christ and the goods of his kingdom of grace. See there the pressure of his love; he would want to become a banishment from Christ for them: *If it were possible that through my destruction Christ could be glorified and the Jews saved, I would not refuse it; for I would wish, if it were possible, if it were permitted, if this choice were given to me; what do you desire but to be separated from Christ, so that all Israel might be united with Christ; Christ glorified, and all the promises of God the Father fulfilled.*

### HOOK, FISHHOOK, <note>original Hebrew: סיר דוגה (*sir dugah*), חכה / חח (*chakkah / chach*); Greek: ἄγκιστρον (*ankistron*), κέντρον (*kentron*); Latin: *hamus*, *hamus piscatorius*</note>

<margin>Shape of the Hooks.</margin> HOOKS are not always prepared from the same material, but are usually curved, and with one or more barbs, which being covered with some bait, and tied and fastened to a cord or line, and attached to some reed or other hand-stick, are let down into the water to deceive and catch the little fish: a matter and practice too well known to make a broad description of it. In Ovid, one reads of it in the 15th book of the *Metamorphoses*:

> *Do not hide the curved hooks with deceptive baits.* <note>original Latin: *Nec celate cibis uncos fallacibus hamos.*</note>

-> That is: <-

> *Do not hide your hook with deceptive foods.*

Scholars may also consult Ausonius, *Idyll 10.*

From the hooks and fishhooks, which one must constantly have in the water, a proverb is derived to spur someone to diligence, so that he lets no opportunity slip; for one does not know where or when one might sometimes reach his goal: *always let your hook hang.* <note>original Latin: *semper tibi pendeat hamus.*</note> See here on this Erasmus in *Adagia, page 207.* Ovid in his Love Poems:

> *Chance has power everywhere. Let your hook always hang,*
> *Where you least expect it, a fish will be in the whirlpool.*
> <note>original Latin: *Casus ubique valet, semper tibi pendeat hamus, / Quo minimè credis, gurgite piscis erit.*</note>

-> That is: <-

> *Chance has power everywhere. Let your hooks hang.*
> *A fish often hides where you would not seek him.*

-> That is, says Erasmus, <-

*One must always take a trial, and use the opportunity.*

This is used figuratively and metaphorically in the Lord's Word to portray something else: which I shall show following the order of the scriptural passages.

*Job 40:20 <note>In many English Bibles, this is Job 41:1.</note> Can you draw the Leviathan with a hook?* I do not intend to determine here what is to be understood by the Leviathan; that belongs to its literal sense: one draws a common fish from the water with the hook, but man does not have the power to do so with the monster (the Leviathan). This one is too large, heavy, and powerful for him: man's dominion finds

<column-break/>

its bridle in this matter: but even that terrible sea monster stands under God's control. *Ps. 104:26, 27.*

*Isa. 19:8. All who cast a hook into the streams shall mourn.* The great Campegius Vitringa <note>A famous Dutch theologian (1659–1722) known for his commentary on Isaiah.</note> writing on Isaiah, says specifically on this passage that it portrays the reduction of Egypt's prosperity, the stripping of their treasures and powers, along with the sadness and grief of the common mass of Egyptians because of this disaster and decay.

That also the Nile stream being dried up and emptied is an allusive portrayal of the Egyptian Power, brought under the authority and control of harsh rulers, and thus oppressed, exhausted, and robbed of goods: and that the persons were of two kinds who drew profit from the Nile stream, the rivers, ponds, and creeks.

That by the fishermen in general one can well understand the people of greater authority, honor, and status, such as governors, leaders in civil life, and in war, who sought to scrape from the wealth and ready Egyptian income, and to drag as much as they could into their own nests: who also had others on hand who could serve their purpose in this, like net-preparers—the lesser sort of people, their servants and subordinate officials.

However, in a more elevated sense, by these fishermen can be understood such persons who through art, craftiness, and deceit knew how to draw the readiest powers and incomes of the Egyptian kingdom to themselves, and to bring them into their possession; such as that Egyptian sort of people whom one calls priests, proponents of false religion, soothsayers, fat priests <note>original Dutch: *vette paapen*, a common derogatory term in the 17th/18th century for wealthy or corrupt clergy</note>, scribes or writers, etc., of which sort and kind there was an infinite number in Egypt. All these fished in the Nile stream, that is, with art and cunning, for the sake of gain, they drew the abundance and means of Egypt to themselves without much trouble and labor: they drew the people and the goods of the people to themselves; for, just as Egypt is figuratively called the Nile, so both Egypt's abundance and the people are compared to fish, even as in *Ezek. 29:4, 5* and *Matt. 4:19.* And they brought these people under their control through their teachings and superstition, as if by a certain bait or by their authority; and in so doing they obtained great treasures, made distinguished profit, and could live and exist excellently.

How it is understood by Coccejus, Calvin, and others, one can consult in Coccejus, Calvin, Calovius, Poole, etc.

The passage *Jer. 16:16. looks at fish and fishermen.* I notice indeed that some have understood these fishermen to be the Chaldeans, who, just as a fisherman plucks the fish out of the water by his hook, would likewise pluck the Jews out of Canaan by their power and carry them away captive: but I have also been able to notice that others have preferred to apply it to the Apostles and their fellow-laborers, spiritual fishers of men, *Ezek. 47:10, Matt. 4:18,* etc., but more on that at a later opportunity.

<margin>Jeremiah 16:16.</margin>

<margin>Amos 4:2.</margin> *Amos 4:2. I read: The Lord has sworn by his holiness that, behold, days shall come upon you, that they shall take you up with hooks, and your descendants with fishhooks.*

The judgment is announced and shown to those of Samaria, that it [will happen] to the Lord, however strongly and firmly nested they might judge themselves to be—
